title: Why Old English forms vary: a short sound history
status: accepted after independent content and complete export review
user_requirement: Optional appendix on breaking, umlaut and related historical processes for readers with linguistic interests, drawing on early Cook and Fulk throughout.
audience: Adult course reader; ordinary grammatical terminology, with historical terms defined locally. No historical-linguistics prerequisite.

scope.answer_key: Not applicable: explanatory prose and worked comparisons, no learner tasks.
scope.length_target: Approximately 8–12 pages, subject to clear complete treatment rather than padding or a hard cap.
scope.notation: No new IPA required. Define front/back/rounding, length/weight, j, starred reconstruction and arrow notation in plain words.

outline.title: Reading a historical explanation
outline.purpose: Set optional scope; distinguish sound history, spelling, a paradigm alternation and reconstruction. Define vowel front/back and rounding in plain words; refer to the pronunciation guide rather than repeat it.

outline.title: Fronting and restoration
outline.purpose: Prepare the changes behind æ/a and why a following syllable can matter; state chronological and West Saxon limits.

outline.title: Breaking
outline.purpose: Explain a front vowel acquiring a second element in the relevant consonant environments; give a compact source-qualified rule and examples. Distinguish the letters ea/eo from a claim of identical origins.

outline.title: i-umlaut
outline.purpose: Explain anticipation of a following i/j, the later loss/change of that trigger, and surviving results in nouns, derivation, comparison and present singulars. Compare long and short results; avoid an unrestricted conversion table.

outline.title: Other origins of diphthong spellings
outline.purpose: Separate back mutation from breaking and palatal diphthongization; include a short paragraph on smoothing with an exactly sourced dialectal example if useful.
outline.open_source_need: A verified smoothing example may need an additive form route to an existing headword.

outline.title: Consonants and the order of changes
outline.purpose: Explain palatalization, selected exceptions produced by chronology, and gemination in plain articulatory terms. Distinguish consonant changes from changes in the following vowel.

outline.title: Vowel loss, syllable weight and contraction
outline.purpose: Connect historical final vowel loss and internal syncope with familiar paradigms; keep long vowel and heavy syllable distinct. Treat contraction as a bounded additional mechanism.

outline.title: Ablaut, inherited alternations and analogy
outline.priority: core distinction; short optional consonant note
outline.purpose: Separate inherited strong stem alternation from conditioned umlaut; explain why analogy or suppletion can prevent a complete surface derivation. No reconstruction of the entire Indo-European or Germanic system.

outline.title: Reference summary and source notes
outline.purpose: One compact table: process, historical trigger, familiar result, principal limitation. Source-specific notes give Cook/Fulk sections and actual printed/PDF pages. Provide optional further-reading pointers.

example_selection: Contracted pool with core comparisons; label all actual used forms and meanings. Record unused groups/extra examples in a final reconciliation.
presentation_rules: Every OE, reconstructed or comparative example and every cited letter/ending is bold; explanatory English terms are italic. Classify every bold span in the final inventory.
Literal reconstruction stars are escaped inside bold, e.g. **\*hælp**. The local star convention differs from Unit3 erroneous-form notation.
Use historical arrows only for actual source-supported development; use beside or labelled columns for coexisting forms.
Use clear prose and compact common-style tables. A comparison table does not introduce a new inflectional class.
Give source citations in endnotes, keeping source apparatus out of the explanation except where the distinction matters.
Preserve all course quantity marks and Cook notation. Do not silently replace the accepted pronunciation convention.

glossary_access.method: Additive route ledger for every actually used OE form and separately classified non-OE/stem/letter item. Existing headwords cover the selected words; show headword access beside new source spellings.
glossary_access.protected_glossary: Keep the original 38-master audit and every accepted glossary artifact unchanged. No new tasks require English-glossary additions.

completion_gates: Save this reconciled contract locally before authoring.

Complete Markdown/TeX/PDF text and table parity; clean compile diagnostics; actually inspect every PDF page.
